plan.estimand: Omnibus F-test power in balanced one-way ANOVA with 3 groups, common variance, and population eta-squared = 0.08
plan.hypothesis: H0: all group means equal; H1: at least one group mean differs
assumptions: Population eta-squared as effect size metric
scientific_notes: Eta-squared = 0.08 represents a small-to-medium effect in ANOVA context
Power calculation uses non-centrality parameter derived from eta-squared and sample sizes
Balanced design with n=25 per group across k=3 groups

answer.summary: The omnibus F-test power for a balanced one-way ANOVA with 3 independent normal groups, total sample size 75 (n=25 per group), population eta-squared 0.08, and significance level α=0.05 is 0.603118 (approximately 60.31%). This result is verified by both analytical calculation using the non-central F distribution and Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 replications, empirical power 0.611, 95% CI [0.601, 0.621]).
answer.method: Non-centrality parameter approach using the non-central F distribution. The non-centrality parameter λ was computed as λ = η²·N/(1−η²) = 0.08×75/0.92 = 6.5217. Power is P(F > F_crit) where F_crit = 3.1239 (critical value from F(2,72) at α=0.05) and F follows a non-central F(2,72) distribution with λ=6.5217. Monte Carlo verification used 10,000 replications with data generated to achieve population η²=0.08 (verified analytically), testing the omnibus F-test at α=0.05.
assumptions: Balanced design with n=25 per group (k=3 groups, N=75 total)
Three independent groups from normal distributions
Common variance across all groups (homogeneity of variance)
Population eta-squared η²=0.08 is the true omnibus effect size
Omnibus F-test for overall differences in group means
limitations: Result assumes all ANOVA assumptions perfectly satisfied; violations of normality, homogeneity of variance, or independence may alter actual power
Does not account for multiple comparisons corrections if conducting follow-up pairwise tests
Assumes η²=0.08 is known precisely; uncertainty in effect size not reflected in the calculation
Exact balancing (25 per group) assumed; unequal group sizes would require different methodology
Monte Carlo CI width (~0.019) reflects finite simulation replication; true power lies within this interval with 95% confidence

# One-way ANOVA power calculation
# Given: k=3 groups, N=75 total (n=25 per group), eta-squared=0.08, alpha=0.05

# Parameters
k <- 3                # number of groups
N <- 75              # total sample size
n_per_group <- N / k # balanced design
eta_squared <- 0.08  # population effect size
alpha <- 0.05        # significance level

# Relationship between eta-squared and non-centrality parameter
# eta_squared = lambda / (lambda + N)
# where lambda is the non-centrality parameter
# Solving for lambda:
# lambda = eta_squared * N / (1 - eta_squared)

lambda <- (eta_squared * N) / (1 - eta_squared)

# Degrees of freedom
df_numerator <- k - 1  # between groups
df_denominator <- N - k  # within groups (error)

# Critical F-value at alpha level
F_critical <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_denominator)

# Power is P(F > F_critical) under the alternative
# Using non-central F distribution
power <- 1 - pf(F_critical, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_denominator, ncp = lambda)

cat("One-Way ANOVA Power Calculation\n")
cat("================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of groups (k): %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("Total sample size (N): %d\n", N))
cat(sprintf("Per-group sample size (n): %d\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("Population eta-squared: %.4f\n", eta_squared))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (alpha): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("\nNon-centrality parameter (lambda): %.4f\n", lambda))
cat(sprintf("Numerator df (between): %d\n", df_numerator))
cat(sprintf("Denominator df (error): %d\n", df_denominator))
cat(sprintf("Critical F-value: %.4f\n", F_critical))
cat(sprintf("\nOmnibus F-test Power: %.6f\n", power))

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = round(power, 15),
  unit = "probability"
)

cat("\n\nStructured Result:\n")
print(results)

# Format for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

library(pwr)

# Parameters
k <- 3                # number of groups
N <- 75              # total sample size
n_per_group <- N / k # balanced design
eta_squared <- 0.08  # population effect size
alpha <- 0.05        # significance level

# Cohen's f is related to eta-squared by:
# eta_squared = f^2 / (1 + f^2)
# Therefore: f = sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))

f <- sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))

cat("Effect Size Conversion\n")
cat("======================\n")
cat(sprintf("Eta-squared: %.4f\n", eta_squared))
cat(sprintf("Cohen's f: %.6f\n", f))

cat("\n\nPower Analysis Result (pwr package)\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(result)

cat("\n\nExtracted Power: ")
power_pwr <- result$power
print(power_pwr)

cat("============================================\n")

df_denominator <- N - k

cat(sprintf("pwr package power:        %.15f\n", power_pwr))
cat(sprintf("Difference: %.2e\n", abs(power_manual - power_pwr)))

# Monte Carlo simulation to verify power
set.seed(42)

k <- 3                # number of groups
n_per_group <- 25     # per-group sample size
N <- k * n_per_group  # total sample size
eta_squared <- 0.08
alpha <- 0.05

# Number of simulations
n_sims <- 10000

# We need to generate data with the specified eta-squared
# eta_squared = SS_between / SS_total
# 
# Strategy: Generate three groups with different means
# If all have variance σ², and means differ, we can calculate eta-squared
# Let's set within-group variance = 1, and adjust means to get desired eta-squared
#
# With group means μ₁, μ₂, μ₃ and grand mean μ_grand:
# η² = Σnᵢ(μᵢ - μ_grand)² / (Σnᵢ(μᵢ - μ_grand)² + Σnᵢσ²)
#
# For symmetric case with 3 groups and equal n:
# If we use a simple pattern: μ₁ = -d, μ₂ = 0, μ₃ = d, then μ_grand = 0
# η² = (2n·d²) / (2n·d² + 3n) = 2d² / (2d² + 3)
# Solving for d: 2d² = η²(2d² + 3)
#              2d²(1 - η²) = 3η²
#              d² = 3η² / (2(1-η²))

sigma_within <- 1  # within-group std dev
d_squared <- (3 * eta_squared) / (2 * (1 - eta_squared))
d <- sqrt(d_squared)

# Group means
mu1 <- -d
mu2 <- 0
mu3 <- d

cat("Data Generation Setup\n")
cat("====================\n")
cat(sprintf("σ (within-group): %.6f\n", sigma_within))
cat(sprintf("Group 1 mean: %.6f\n", mu1))
cat(sprintf("Group 2 mean: %.6f\n", mu2))
cat(sprintf("Group 3 mean: %.6f\n", mu3))
cat(sprintf("d: %.6f\n", d))

# Verify eta-squared in population
grand_mean <- (mu1 + mu2 + mu3) / 3
ss_between_pop <- n_per_group * ((mu1 - grand_mean)^2 + (mu2 - grand_mean)^2 + (mu3 - grand_mean)^2)
ss_within_pop <- k * n_per_group * sigma_within^2
ss_total_pop <- ss_between_pop + ss_within_pop
eta_sq_check <- ss_between_pop / ss_total_pop

cat(sprintf("\nVerification - Population eta-squared: %.6f (target: %.6f)\n", eta_sq_check, eta_squared))

# Run simulations
reject_count <- 0

for (i in 1:n_sims) {
  # Generate data
  group1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = mu1, sd = sigma_within)
  group2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = mu2, sd = sigma_within)
  group3 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = mu3, sd = sigma_within)
  
  # Combine into data frame
  data <- data.frame(
    value = c(group1, group2, group3),
    group = factor(rep(1:3, each = n_per_group))
  )
  
  # Fit ANOVA
  aov_result <- aov(value ~ group, data = data)
  
  # Extract F-statistic and p-value
  f_stat <- summary(aov_result)[[1]]$`F value`[1]
  p_value <- summary(aov_result)[[1]]$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  
  # Check if null is rejected at alpha level
  if (!is.na(p_value) && p_value < alpha) {
    reject_count <- reject_count + 1
  }
}

power_mc <- reject_count / n_sims
se_power <- sqrt(power_mc * (1 - power_mc) / n_sims)

cat("\n\nMonte Carlo Simulation Results\n")
cat("==============================\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of simulations: %d\n", n_sims))
cat(sprintf("Rejections at α=%.4f: %d\n", alpha, reject_count))
cat(sprintf("Empirical power: %.6f\n", power_mc))
cat(sprintf("Standard error: %.6f\n", se_power))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.6f, %.6f]\n", power_mc - 1.96*se_power, power_mc + 1.96*se_power))

# Compare to theoretical
theoretical_power <- 0.6031178831465038
cat(sprintf("\nTheoretical power: %.6f\n", theoretical_power))
cat(sprintf("Difference: %.6f\n", abs(power_mc - theoretical_power)))
cat(sprintf("Z-score: %.4f\n", (power_mc - theoretical_power) / se_power))

jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  results = list(list(metric = "power", value = theoretical_power, unit = "probability")),
  simulation = list(
    seed = 42,
    trials = n_sims,
    failures = 0,
    mcse = se_power,
    confidence_interval = c(power_mc - 1.96*se_power, power_mc + 1.96*se_power)
  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

alpha <- 0.05

#

#

# η² = (2n·d²) / (2n·d² + 3n) = 2d² / (2d² + 3)

#              d² = 3η² / (2(1-η²))

mu2 <- 0
mu3 <- d

eta_sq_check <- ss_between_pop / ss_total_pop

# Evidence e1; success=true

# One-way ANOVA power calculation
# Given: k=3 groups, N=75 total (n=25 per group), eta-squared=0.08, alpha=0.05

# Parameters
k <- 3                # number of groups
N <- 75              # total sample size
n_per_group <- N / k # balanced design
eta_squared <- 0.08  # population effect size
alpha <- 0.05        # significance level

# Relationship between eta-squared and non-centrality parameter
# eta_squared = lambda / (lambda + N)
# where lambda is the non-centrality parameter
# Solving for lambda:
# lambda = eta_squared * N / (1 - eta_squared)

lambda <- (eta_squared * N) / (1 - eta_squared)

# Degrees of freedom
df_numerator <- k - 1  # between groups
df_denominator <- N - k  # within groups (error)

# Critical F-value at alpha level
F_critical <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_denominator)

# Power is P(F > F_critical) under the alternative
# Using non-central F distribution
power <- 1 - pf(F_critical, df1 = df_numerator, df2 = df_denominator, ncp = lambda)

cat("One-Way ANOVA Power Calculation\n")
cat("================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of groups (k): %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("Total sample size (N): %d\n", N))
cat(sprintf("Per-group sample size (n): %d\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("Population eta-squared: %.4f\n", eta_squared))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (alpha): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("\nNon-centrality parameter (lambda): %.4f\n", lambda))
cat(sprintf("Numerator df (between): %d\n", df_numerator))
cat(sprintf("Denominator df (error): %d\n", df_denominator))
cat(sprintf("Critical F-value: %.4f\n", F_critical))
cat(sprintf("\nOmnibus F-test Power: %.6f\n", power))

# Output for structured reporting

  metric = "power",
  value = round(power, 15),
  unit = "probability"
)

)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  results = list(list(metric = "power", value = theoretical_power, unit = "probability")),
  simulation = list(
    seed = 42,
    trials = n_sims,
    failures = 0,
    mcse = se_power,
    confidence_interval = c(ci_lower, ci_upper)
  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

cat(paste("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", POWER_AGENT_RESULT, "\n", sep = ""))
